name: Gwynn ap Nudd

attributes.attribute: The Welsh king of Fairyland, called the White One, son of the Dark.
He ruled the Tylwyth Teg, tiny folk in blue who danced by night.
At Beltane he led the Wild Hunt to raid the land of the living.
His father was king of Annwn and his queen was Creiddylad.
She was the basis for Shakespeare's character Cordelia.
Alternative names include Herne the Hunter and Gabriel.

sources: Evans-Wentz, W. Y. The Fairy-Faith in Celtic Countries. Gerrards Cross: Colin Smythe Humanities Press, 1911, 152 ff.
Lonigan, Paul R. *The Druids: Priests of the Ancient Celts.* Contributions to the Study of Religion, no. 45. Westport, Conn.: Greenwood Press, 1996, 169.
Spence, Lewis. The Minor Traditions of British Mythology. (New York: Benjamin Blom, Inc., 1972), 109.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Gwynn ap Nudd, the White One, son of the Dark, was the Welsh king of Fairyland. He lived beneath Glastonbury Tor and ruled the Tylwyth Teg, tiny folk in blue who danced by night. At Beltane, the start of spring, he led the Wild Hunt to raid the land of the living. He could appear at will amid fairy music. His father was king of Annwn, a Hades-like Otherworld, and his queen was Creiddylad, the basis for Shakespeare's Cordelia. Some call him Herne the Hunter or Gabriel.

okr.objective: Describe Gwynn ap Nudd as the Welsh king of Fairyland who led the Wild Hunt at Beltane.
